title: Scheduled job runs hang on writefile's modal save dialog (unattended-run gate missing)
existing_state: writefile pops a modal "Choose Save Location" dialog whenever the resolved path is not fully qualified (Services/Scripting/Commands/WriteFileCommand.cs:175-184 calls _savePathPrompt -> ScriptPromptDialogRunner at :187-193) with no check of `context.AllowFileSelectionDialogs`. The sibling readfile command DOES gate its picker on that flag (ReadFileCommand.cs:237-238, throwing a clear manual-only message), and JobExecutionService explicitly forces the flag off for scheduler and Run-Now job executions (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:687 and :744 pass allowFileSelectionDialogs: false, threaded into the context at SshExecutionService.cs:1771). Result: a scheduled job whose script contains `writefile: { path: output.txt }` (or a path built from a variable that resolves relative) blocks mid-run on a dialog nobody is there to click — the job stalls indefinitely — or pops a modal over the user's desktop mid-meeting. There is even an unattended preflight mechanism for localcmd (SshExecutionService.cs:939-942, TryBuildUnattendedLocalCmdPreflightMessage) that writefile is not part of.
recommendation: Mirror the readfile gate: in WriteFileCommand.ResolveFilePathAsync, if the path is not fully qualified and !context.AllowFileSelectionDialogs, fail the step with a clear message ("relative writefile paths require a manual run — use an absolute path in scheduled jobs") instead of prompting. Optionally also extend the unattended preflight (TryBuildUnattendedLocalCmdPreflightMessage pattern) to detect relative writefile paths before the run starts.
user_benefit: Scheduled jobs no longer silently stall forever (or surprise-popup on the desktop) because of a relative output path; the failure becomes an actionable error in job history.

evidence.note: ResolveFilePathAsync prompts on any non-fully-qualified path; no AllowFileSelectionDialogs check
readfile's gate — the established pattern writefile is missing
scheduler/job runs pass allowFileSelectionDialogs: false — proving the unattended scenario is real and intended to be dialog-free
